chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you stand in prayer, do not play with your beard, nor with your head, nor with the pebbles while you are praying, unless you level them where you will prostrate, for there is no harm.
ai.seo_question: What movements invalidate or detract from the humility of prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the principle of *khushu'* (humility) by prohibiting distracting, frivolous movements (*tabathul*) with the beard, head, or pebbles during prayer. It specifically permits adjusting the prostration surface only to the extent necessary for proper *sujood*, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on balancing physical composure with ritual validity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you stand regarding the Salāt, so neither play around with your beard, nor with your head, nor with the pebbles while you are praying Salāt, unless you prepare (pebbles) as you are about to do Sajdah, so it is not a problem’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when you stand up for Salah (prayer), you must not play with your beard, your head or with pebbles while you pray, except when you prepare (pebbles) as you are about to do sajdah in which case it is not an offense.”
